maxine-waters.text: Sponsored the Ending Homelessness Act of 2025 (H.R. 4872) and the Housing Crisis Response Act of 2025 (H.R. 6771); backed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act (H.R. 6644, June 2026), including limits on large institutional investors buying single-family homes.

Applauded a federal court ruling that temporarily blocked the Trump administration from suspending the Los Angeles Homeless Services Authority from federal homelessness grant programs (Aug. 14, 2026 press release).
Cosponsored the Medicare for All Act (H.R. 3069) and introduced bills for diabetes care grants and maternal and infant health services in underserved communities.
Opposes offshore oil drilling off California's coast, supports U.S. participation in the Paris Climate Agreement, opposes EPA budget cuts, and supports zero-emission transit.
Cosponsored the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025 (H.R. 3115) and took part in the 2016 House Democratic sit-in demanding votes on gun-control legislation.

Opposes mass-deportation policies and federal targeting of sanctuary cities (May 28, 2026 release); cosponsored the Keep Families Together Act and the Haitian Refugee Immigration Fairness Act of 2026.
Opposes efforts to restrict mail-in voting and shift election control to the federal government; criticized federal use of government data to verify voter eligibility (May 28, 2026 press release).
Voted for the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act (H.R. 1280): 'Today, in honor of every person who was taken from us too soon, I voted in favor of the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act.'

source.title: Waters Statement on Passage of the George Floyd Justice in Policing Act

maxine-waters.text: Co-introduced the Workforce Justice Act (2021) to push states to 'ban the box' by removing criminal-history questions from job applications until after a conditional offer, for public and private employers.

source.title: Waters, Trone Introduce Legislation to Ban the Box

maxine-waters.text: Co-introduced legislation protecting small businesses from anti-competitive pricing (Fair Competition Act for Small Businesses, Dec. 2025).

cristian-morales.text: Says jobs and housing are the district's top issues; wants to bring businesses and jobs back to California and address barriers to homeownership.
Says Medicaid and Medicare should remain available but no other taxpayer-funded health care programs are necessary.
Says California regulations impose excessive costs on businesses, favors developing nuclear or lower-emission energy, and says innovation could reduce the need for regulations.
Prioritizes applicants who follow legal immigration processes and strongly disagrees with sanctuary cities.
Supports the individual right to bear arms and opposes ownership restrictions justified as public safety measures.
Says human life deserves legal protection from conception; would allow elective abortion only for rape, incest, or the mother's life; strongly disagrees with public funding for abortion providers.
Opposes transgender women in women's sports and in designated women's spaces such as bathrooms, locker rooms, shelters, and prisons.
Strongly agrees with eliminating the U.S. Department of Education, returning control to states and communities, and supporting school choice for parents.
Supports requiring voter photo ID, a federal Election Day holiday, and counting all votes the same day; says states should keep election administration.
Lists combating crime and improving conditions in Compton and Watts among his priorities; says he favors pro-labor Republican economic policies and bringing manufacturing jobs back to California.
Endorsed by the California Republican Party.
